location: A-S, A 29/2 (Geir. 179****); acquired in 1867 from Stift Bayerisch-Laufen****.
signature: “MACHT . IOHANN . CARL . KODISCH . IN . NVRNBERG 1687”; master’s mark: prancing horse with bit and raised tail, above initials “ICK”.
dimensions: bo 12,¹  be 125,  le 3565,³  h 1340,⁴  mouthpipe diam. 10.5
literature: Geiringer 1932: 30; Birsak 1977: 29, tafel XII (photo); Langwill 1980: 93; Waterhouse 1993: 209; ****Birsak 2004???
remarks: Parts of two different instruments. Tubular slide stays; hinged handle with ivory grip (280mm long) attached to moveable slide stay. Bell sec. from a tenor trombone. [****If bell is from a tenor, it ties for the largest tenor bell of the period 1650-99.] Flat bell-stay, with hinge, eyelet toward bell-pipe side. Bell somewhat dented. Between orig. bell and bell-bow, piece of tubing 420mm long, of rough workmanship, inserted. Garland has floral design and six cast angels’ heads with wings. Nuremberg-style garland 35mm wide, engraved blossom pattern between words of signature. Flat bell stay, engraved. Ring in slide-bow and bell-bow.
